$description: Reading plans on the Learn tab. The day splits are computed by pipeline/courses.py; `days` holds the words for each computed day, in order (written for Pax). Keep slugs stable.

courses.title: Bible in a Year
courses.summary: The whole story of salvation, about 15 minutes a day
courses.intro: Read all 73 books of the Bible in a year, in the order the story unfolds: from creation through the patriarchs, the exodus, the kingdom, exile and return, to Jesus and the early Church. Each day has a passage of about three chapters, plus a Psalm or a few Proverbs to pray with. Start any day. If you miss a day, the plan simply waits for you.

sections.name: Beginnings
sections.intro: Creation, the fall, the flood and Babel: the opening chapters of Genesis set the stage for everything that follows. God makes a good world, we break it, and God begins at once to rescue us.

sections.name: The Patriarchs
sections.intro: God calls Abraham and promises that through his family all nations will be blessed. The promise passes to Isaac, Jacob and Joseph, through rivalry, famine and forgiveness. Job, a story set in the same ancient world, asks why the innocent suffer.

sections.name: Egypt and the Exodus
sections.intro: Abraham's descendants are slaves in Egypt. God frees them through Moses, makes a covenant with them at Sinai, gives them the Law and the way to worship, and leads them through forty years in the desert to the edge of the promised land.

sections.name: The Promised Land
sections.intro: Joshua leads Israel into Canaan. Then comes the age of the judges, a cycle of forgetting God, suffering and being rescued, and the quiet faithfulness of Ruth, the great-grandmother of King David.

sections.name: The Kingdom
sections.intro: Israel asks for a king. Saul, David and Solomon reign over a united kingdom, and God promises David a son whose kingdom will last forever. Solomon builds the Temple. The Song of Songs and Ecclesiastes come from the wisdom of this age.

sections.name: A Kingdom Divided
sections.intro: After Solomon the kingdom splits in two, Israel in the north and Judah in the south. Kings rise and fall, and prophets such as Elijah, Isaiah and Jeremiah call the people back to God. Assyria destroys the north; Babylon takes Jerusalem.

sections.name: Exile
sections.intro: In Babylon, far from the Temple, God does not abandon his people. Ezekiel sees God's glory, Daniel stays faithful at a pagan court, and the second half of Isaiah announces comfort, a new exodus and a suffering servant.

sections.name: Return
sections.intro: Persia lets the exiles go home. They rebuild the Temple and the walls of Jerusalem under Ezra and Nehemiah, encouraged by the last prophets. Esther and Judith show God protecting his people through unlikely heroes.

sections.name: The Maccabees and Wisdom
sections.intro: Greek rulers try to stamp out the faith, and the Maccabee family leads a revolt to save the Temple. Wisdom and Sirach gather Israel's wisdom on the eve of Christ's coming, and even hint at life after death.

sections.name: The Messiah
sections.intro: The four Gospels tell how God's promises come true in Jesus: his birth, his teaching and miracles, his death and resurrection. Read them as four portraits of one Lord.

sections.name: The Church
sections.intro: The risen Jesus sends the Holy Spirit, and the Church spreads from Jerusalem to Rome. Acts tells the story, and the letters of Paul, Peter, James, John and Jude are read where they fit in it. Revelation closes the Bible with the victory of the Lamb.

days.title: Creation and the Fall
days.intro: God speaks and creation comes to be, good in every part, with man and woman made in his image. Then come the serpent’s lie, the first sin and exile from the garden. Watch for God’s promise of victory over the serpent, and for Cain’s jealousy turning to murder.
days.question: Where do you most need to trust God’s goodness instead of grasping for control?

days.title: Noah and the Flood
days.intro: A long family line runs from Adam to Noah, including Enoch, who walked with God. As wickedness fills the earth, God tells Noah to build an ark. The waters rise and fall, a dove returns with an olive leaf, and Noah offers sacrifice.
days.question: What helps you stay faithful when the people around you are not?

days.title: The Rainbow and Babel
days.intro: God blesses Noah and makes a covenant with every living thing, sealed by the rainbow. Noah’s sons spread across the earth. At Babel people try to build a tower reaching heaven, and God scatters their languages. The reading ends with Abram’s family line.
days.question: Where are you tempted to make a name for yourself rather than seek God?

days.title: Abram Is Called
days.intro: God calls Abram to leave home and promises him land, descendants and blessing for all nations. Abram parts from Lot, rescues him, and receives bread and wine from Melchizedek. He believes God, yet he and Sarai try to hurry the promise through Hagar.
days.question: What is God asking you to leave behind in order to follow him?

days.title: The Covenant and Sodom
days.intro: God renames Abram and Sarai as Abraham and Sarah and gives circumcision as the sign of his covenant. Three visitors promise a son, and Sarah laughs. Abraham bargains with God for Sodom. Angels rescue Lot’s family, but Lot’s wife looks back.
days.question: For whom could you plead with God, boldly, as Abraham did?

days.title: The Testing of Abraham
days.intro: Isaac is finally born and Sarah laughs for joy, while Hagar and Ishmael are sent away yet cared for by God. Then God tests Abraham, asking for his beloved son on a mountain. Watch Abraham’s trust and God’s provision of a ram. Sarah dies and is buried.
days.question: What gift from God do you find hardest to hold with open hands?

days.title: A Wife for Isaac
days.intro: Abraham’s servant travels to Abraham’s kin to find a wife for Isaac, praying for a sign at the well. Rebekah answers with generous kindness and agrees to go. Abraham dies. Rebekah bears twins, Esau and Jacob, and Esau trades his birthright for a bowl of stew.
days.question: When have you seen God answer a simple, honest prayer for guidance?

days.title: Jacob Takes the Blessing
days.intro: God renews his promise to Isaac, who digs wells and makes peace with Abimelech after quarrels over water. Then, urged by Rebekah, Jacob disguises himself as Esau to receive his blind father’s blessing. Esau’s grief turns to rage, and Jacob must flee.
days.question: Where are you tempted to grab what God might give in his own time?

days.title: Jacob’s Ladder
days.intro: Fleeing Esau, Jacob dreams of a ladder reaching heaven with angels on it, and God renews the promise to him at Bethel. In Haran he loves Rachel, but Laban tricks him into marrying Leah first. Rivalry between the sisters fills the house with children.
days.question: Where has God met you in a place you did not expect him?

days.title: Jacob Wrestles with God
days.intro: Jacob slips away from Laban with his family and flocks, while Rachel hides her father’s idols. Laban overtakes them, and they make a covenant. Afraid of meeting Esau, Jacob prays and sends gifts ahead. At night he wrestles until dawn and receives the name Israel.
days.question: What struggle with God are you being asked to stay with until morning?

days.title: Brothers Reconciled
days.intro: Esau runs to embrace Jacob, and the brothers make peace. At Shechem, Dinah is violated, and Simeon and Levi take brutal revenge. God sends Jacob back to Bethel, and the family puts away its idols. Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, and Isaac dies.
days.question: Is there someone you need to meet with forgiveness, as Esau met Jacob?

days.title: Joseph Sold by His Brothers
days.intro: A record of Esau’s descendants, the people of Edom, comes first. Then the story turns to Joseph, Jacob’s favorite son, with his special coat and his dreams. His jealous brothers plot against him, throw him into a pit and sell him to traders bound for Egypt.
days.question: Where has envy or favoritism caused harm in your family or friendships?

days.title: Judah, Tamar and Joseph
days.intro: Judah wrongs his daughter-in-law Tamar, who bears twins, Perez and Zerah, and Judah admits she is more just than he is. In Egypt, Joseph serves Potiphar faithfully, refuses his master’s wife, and is jailed on a false charge. There he explains two dreams, then is forgotten.
days.question: How do you stay faithful when doing right seems to bring only trouble?

days.title: Joseph Rules Egypt
days.intro: Pharaoh’s dreams of fat and thin cows trouble him, and Joseph explains them: seven years of plenty, then seven of famine. Pharaoh sets him over Egypt. When famine reaches Canaan, Joseph’s brothers come to buy grain and bow before him, not knowing who he is.
days.question: How has God used a hard season to prepare you for something later?

days.title: Benjamin and the Silver Cup
days.intro: The brothers return to Egypt with Benjamin, and Joseph hosts them, weeping in private. He hides his silver cup in Benjamin’s sack to test them. Watch Judah, who once urged selling Joseph, now offer himself as a slave in his young brother’s place.
days.question: Where could you offer yourself for someone else’s good, as Judah did?

days.title: Joseph Reveals Himself
days.intro: Joseph can hold back no longer and tells his brothers who he is, saying God sent him ahead to save lives. Jacob, encouraged by God in a vision, brings the whole family to Egypt. They settle in Goshen, while the famine drives the Egyptians to sell their land to Pharaoh.
days.question: What past pain might God be weaving into a story of rescue?

days.title: Jacob’s Blessing and Joseph’s Mercy
days.intro: Jacob blesses Joseph’s sons, crossing his hands to favor the younger. On his deathbed he speaks over each of his twelve sons, promising that the scepter will not leave Judah. After his burial, Joseph assures his fearful brothers that God turned their evil into good.
days.question: Is there someone you need to reassure of your forgiveness, as Joseph did?

days.title: Job Loses Everything
days.intro: Job is upright and richly blessed. Satan claims Job serves God only for gain, and God permits him to be tested. Job loses his children, goods and health, yet does not curse God. His friends sit with him in silence, then Job curses his birth and Eliphaz replies.
days.question: What would remain of your faith if your comforts were taken away?

days.title: Eliphaz and Job’s Reply
days.intro: Eliphaz urges Job to accept God’s correction and repent, sure that suffering must point to sin. Job insists he has done nothing to deserve this and says his friends have let him down. Then he speaks straight to God about the misery of his days.
days.question: When someone you love suffers, do you rush to explain, or simply stay with them?

days.title: Who Can Stand Before God?
days.intro: Bildad tells Job that God never twists justice, so Job’s children must have sinned. Job agrees that no one can win an argument with God, and he longs for someone to stand between them. Then he asks God why he made him with such care only to afflict him.
days.question: What questions would you honestly bring to God if you were not afraid?

days.title: Job Clings to Hope
days.intro: Zophar bluntly calls Job to repent. Job answers that he knows God’s power as well as they do, and that their defense of God is false. He says he will trust God even if God slays him. He reflects on life’s shortness and asks whether the dead will live again.
days.question: What helps you keep hoping in God when his ways make no sense?

days.title: My Witness Is in Heaven
days.intro: Eliphaz and Bildad return with harsher words, describing the dark fate of the wicked and implying Job is one of them. Job calls them troublesome comforters. Yet even near despair, he declares that his witness is in heaven and turns his tear-filled eyes to God.
days.question: Who has been a true comforter to you, and how could you be one?

days.title: I Know My Redeemer Lives
days.intro: Job feels abandoned by family, friends and servants, and begs his friends for pity. Then comes his great confession: he knows his Redeemer lives and that in his flesh he will see God. Zophar describes the ruin of the wicked, and Job answers that the wicked often prosper.
days.question: What difference does it make to you today that your Redeemer lives?

days.title: Where Can I Find God?
days.intro: Eliphaz now falsely accuses Job of cruelty to the poor. Job longs to find God and lay out his case, trusting that God has tried him like gold. He grieves at injustice that seems to go unpunished. Bildad’s short speech asks how any mortal can be just before God.
days.question: When God feels hidden, what keeps you seeking him?

days.title: Where Is Wisdom Found?
days.intro: Job praises God’s power over earth and sky, calling it only a small part of his ways, and refuses to give up his integrity. A poem follows: people dig deep for gold and gems, but wisdom comes from God, and fearing the Lord is wisdom. Then he recalls happier days.
days.question: Where do you go looking for wisdom before you go to God?

days.title: Job’s Final Defense
days.intro: Job contrasts his old honor with the scorn he now endures, even from young men. He swears he has been pure, honest, generous to the poor and free of idolatry, and asks God to answer him. Then young Elihu, angry at Job and his friends, begins to speak.
days.question: If you honestly examined your conscience, what would you want to set right?

days.title: Elihu Speaks
days.intro: Elihu says God speaks to people in dreams and through sickness, to turn them from pride and spare them from the grave. He insists that God never acts wickedly or unjustly, and he rebukes Job for speaking as if being righteous gains a person nothing.
days.question: How might God be speaking to you through a difficulty right now?

days.title: The Lord Answers Job
days.intro: Elihu finishes by praising God’s greatness in rain, thunder and snow. Then the Lord himself answers Job out of a whirlwind. He does not explain Job’s suffering. Instead he asks where Job was when the earth was founded and leads him through the wonders of sea, light and sky.
days.question: What in creation reminds you that God is greater than your understanding?

days.title: Job Is Restored
days.intro: God keeps showing Job the wild creatures he made, from the eagle to Behemoth and Leviathan. Job falls silent and repents in dust and ashes. God says the friends did not speak rightly of him and asks Job to pray for them. Job’s fortunes are restored twice over.
days.question: Who might God be asking you to pray for, even after they hurt you?

days.title: The Burning Bush
days.intro: Jacob’s family has grown into a people, and a new Pharaoh enslaves them and orders their baby boys killed. Moses is saved by his mother and Pharaoh’s daughter, then flees to Midian. At a burning bush, God calls him to free Israel and reveals his name.
days.question: Where is God calling you that you would rather not go?

days.title: Moses Before Pharaoh
days.intro: Moses raises objections, and God gives him signs and his brother Aaron as spokesman. Pharaoh refuses to let the people go and makes them gather their own straw for bricks. The Israelites blame Moses, but God renews his promise to bring them out and make them his people.
days.question: What excuses do you give God when he asks something hard of you?

days.title: The Plagues Begin
days.intro: Aaron’s staff becomes a serpent, and the plagues start: the Nile turned to blood, then frogs, gnats, flies, dead livestock, boils and hail. Pharaoh’s magicians keep up at first but soon fail. Watch Pharaoh promise to release Israel, then harden his heart again and again.
days.question: Have you promised God a change, then hardened your heart once relief came?

days.title: The First Passover
days.intro: Locusts and darkness fall on Egypt, and Pharaoh still refuses. God gives Israel the Passover: a lamb without blemish, its blood on the doorposts, eaten in haste with unleavened bread. At midnight the firstborn of Egypt die, and Israel finally leaves.
days.question: How does the Passover lamb deepen the way you approach the Eucharist?

days.title: Crossing the Red Sea
days.intro: Israel leaves Egypt led by a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night, carrying Joseph’s bones. Pharaoh’s army chases them to the sea. Moses stretches out his hand, the waters part, and Israel crosses on dry ground. Moses and Miriam lead songs of praise.
days.question: What Red Sea has God already brought you through?

days.title: Manna in the Desert
days.intro: The people grumble in the wilderness, so God sends quail and daily manna, with a double portion before the sabbath. Water flows from a rock, and Israel defeats Amalek while Moses’ arms are held up. Jethro advises Moses to share the work. Today’s shepherd psalm fits well.
days.question: What are you anxious about, and can you trust God with just today?

days.title: The Ten Commandments
days.intro: At Sinai, God offers Israel a covenant: they will be his own people, a kingdom of priests. Amid thunder he speaks the Ten Commandments, and the frightened people beg Moses to speak to them. Laws on altars, servants and injuries follow. The psalm asks who may climb the Lord’s mountain.
days.question: Which commandment is God inviting you to live more fully this week?

days.title: The Covenant Sealed
days.intro: More laws guard property, protect the stranger, widow and orphan, and set the yearly feasts. God promises an angel to guide Israel. Then Moses reads the book of the covenant, the people pledge to obey, and he sprinkles them with blood. The elders see God and eat and drink.
days.question: Who is the stranger, widow or orphan God has placed near you?

days.title: Plans for the Tabernacle
days.intro: On the mountain God gives Moses the pattern for a sanctuary, so that he can dwell among his people. Watch for the ark of the covenant with its golden mercy seat and cherubim, the table for the bread of the Presence, the lampstand, the curtains, the altar and the court.
days.question: How do you make room for God to dwell in your daily life?

days.title: Garments for the Priests
days.intro: God orders sacred garments for Aaron and his sons: an ephod, a breastpiece set with twelve stones for the tribes, and a gold plate engraved Holy to the Lord. He then describes the seven days of ordination and the daily offering of a lamb each morning and evening.
days.question: What habit of prayer, morning and evening, could anchor your day?

days.title: The Golden Calf
days.intro: God finishes his instructions: an altar of incense, a basin for washing, holy oil, and Bezalel, filled with God’s spirit, to do the craftwork. Moses receives the stone tablets. Meanwhile the people make a golden calf. Moses pleads for them, breaks the tablets and confronts Aaron.
days.question: What golden calf tempts you when God seems slow or far away?

days.title: Moses Sees God’s Glory
days.intro: After the calf, God speaks with Moses face to face, as with a friend. Moses asks to see his glory and is hidden in a rock as God passes by, proclaiming his mercy. The covenant is renewed, Moses’ face shines, and the people bring gifts for the sanctuary.
days.question: How would your prayer change if you spoke to God as a friend?

days.title: Building the Sanctuary
days.intro: Bezalel, Oholiab and the skilled workers begin. The people give so much that Moses must tell them to stop. Chapter by chapter the plans become real: curtains and boards, the veil, the ark and mercy seat, the table, lampstand, altars and court, with a tally of the metals offered.
days.question: What gift or skill could you offer generously for God’s work?

days.title: The Glory Fills the Tabernacle
days.intro: The priestly garments are finished, and Moses inspects the work and blesses the people. On the first day of the new year the tabernacle is set up and anointed. Then the cloud covers it and the glory of the Lord fills it, so that even Moses cannot enter.
days.question: When have you sensed God’s presence filling an ordinary place?

days.title: Laws of Offerings
days.intro: From the tabernacle God teaches Moses how Israel is to draw near with offerings: whole burnt offerings, grain offerings seasoned with salt, peace offerings shared in fellowship, and sin offerings for wrongs done unknowingly. Notice the worshiper laying a hand on the animal’s head.
days.question: What would it mean to give God your whole self, holding nothing back?

days.title: Making Things Right
days.intro: More offerings cover sins such as failing to testify, touching what is unclean, rash oaths and cheating a neighbor. Wrongs against others require repayment plus a fifth more. Priests learn their share, the altar fire must never go out, and no fat or blood may be eaten.
days.question: Is there a wrong you need not only to confess, but also to repair?

days.title: Aaron’s Ordination
days.intro: Moses washes, clothes and anoints Aaron and his sons, and they stay at the tent for seven days. When Aaron offers his first sacrifices, fire from the Lord consumes them and the people fall on their faces. Then Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire and are struck dead.
days.question: How do you approach holy things, like the Mass, with reverence?

days.title: Clean and Unclean
days.intro: God sets out which animals Israel may eat, calling them to be holy because he is holy. A mother brings an offering after childbirth, with turtledoves allowed for the poor. Then come detailed tests for leprosy in skin and garments, which the priest must examine.
days.question: What does being holy as God is holy look like in your ordinary day?

days.title: Cleansing the Leper
days.intro: A healed leper is restored to the community through a rite with two birds, cedar, scarlet and hyssop, followed by offerings. Rules follow for leprosy in houses and for bodily discharges. These laws keep Israel mindful that God dwells in their midst.
days.question: Who has been left on the edges, and how could you help bring them back?

days.title: The Day of Atonement
days.intro: Once a year the high priest enters the holy of holies with blood to make atonement. One goat is sacrificed, and the other carries the people’s sins away into the wilderness. Blood, the life of the flesh, must not be eaten. Laws on marriage and sexual conduct follow.
days.question: What do you need to let God carry away from you today?

days.title: Be Holy, Love Your Neighbor
days.intro: God calls Israel to be holy as he is holy, and shows what that looks like: leave gleanings for the poor, pay wages promptly, judge fairly, love your neighbor as yourself, and love the stranger too. Penalties for grave sins follow, then special rules for priests.
days.question: Which neighbor are you being asked to love as yourself today?

days.title: Israel’s Holy Feasts
days.intro: Offerings must be without blemish. Then God sets Israel’s calendar: the sabbath, Passover and Unleavened Bread, firstfruits, the feast of Weeks, Trumpets, the Day of Atonement and Tabernacles. Oil keeps the lamp burning, twelve loaves lie before the Lord, and a blasphemer is judged.
days.question: How do you keep Sunday and the Church’s feasts holy?

days.title: The Year of Jubilee
days.intro: Every seventh year the land rests, and every fiftieth year is a jubilee, when land returns to its families and Israelites sold into service go free, for the land belongs to God. Then come blessings for obedience, warnings for rebellion, and God’s promise to remember his covenant when they repent.
days.question: What would it look like to treat what you own as belonging to God?

days.title: Vows and the First Census
days.intro: Leviticus closes with rules for vows, for redeeming what has been dedicated to God, and for the tithe. Numbers opens in the wilderness of Sinai, as Moses counts the men able to fight, tribe by tribe. The Levites are set apart to care for the tabernacle.
days.question: What promise you made to God needs renewing?

days.title: The Camp Around the Tabernacle
days.intro: The tribes camp in order on four sides of the tabernacle, with Judah on the east, so God’s dwelling stands at the center. Aaron’s sons serve as priests. The Levites are counted and given their duties, and God takes them in place of Israel’s firstborn.
days.question: What would change if God were truly at the center of your life?

days.title: The Priestly Blessing
days.intro: Levite clans receive their tasks for carrying the tabernacle, with the holiest things covered first. Laws follow on confession and repayment, a husband’s jealousy, and the Nazirite vow of special dedication. The day ends with the blessing Aaron speaks over Israel: the Lord bless you and keep you.
days.question: Who could you bless today, in word or in prayer?

days.title: Gifts for the Altar
days.intro: When the tabernacle is anointed, the twelve tribal leaders bring offerings, one leader each day for twelve days. Each gift is the same, yet each is recorded in full. At the end, Moses hears God speaking to him from above the mercy seat.
days.question: How does it feel to know God sees even your small, repeated offerings?

days.title: Israel Sets Out
days.intro: The lamps are set up, and the Levites are cleansed and presented to God. Israel keeps the Passover, with a later date for those who were unclean. The cloud over the tabernacle tells the camp when to stay and when to move. Silver trumpets sound, and the people leave Sinai.
days.question: How do you discern when God is asking you to stay or to move?

days.title: Grumbling and the Spies
days.intro: The people crave meat, and Moses feels his burden is too heavy. God shares his spirit with seventy elders and sends quail, followed by a plague. Miriam and Aaron challenge Moses, and Miriam is struck with leprosy. Twelve spies scout Canaan and return with a huge cluster of grapes.
days.question: What do you grumble about that might actually be a gift?

days.title: Forty Years in the Wilderness
days.intro: Frightened by the spies’ report, the people want to go back to Egypt. Only Joshua and Caleb urge trust in God. Moses pleads, and God pardons yet decrees that this generation will wander forty years and die in the desert. Laws follow, including tassels to recall the commandments.
days.question: Where has fear kept you from stepping into what God has promised?

days.title: Korah’s Rebellion
days.intro: Korah, Dathan and Abiram rise against Moses and Aaron, and the earth swallows them. When the people grumble again, Aaron stands with his censer between the dead and the living until the plague stops. Aaron’s staff buds and bears almonds, and the duties of priests and Levites are set.
days.question: How do you respond when you envy someone else’s role or calling?

days.title: The Bronze Serpent
days.intro: A red heifer’s ashes make water for purification. Miriam dies. At Meribah, Moses strikes the rock twice, and God says he will not lead the people into the land. Aaron dies on Mount Hor. When serpents bite the people, those who look at a bronze serpent live.
days.question: When you are wounded by sin, where do you turn your eyes?

days.title: Balaam’s Blessings
days.intro: Balak, king of Moab, hires the seer Balaam to curse Israel. On the way, Balaam’s donkey sees an angel blocking the road and speaks. Three times Balaam tries to curse, and each time only blessing comes out. He foresees a star rising out of Jacob.
days.question: How might God be trying to get your attention, as he did with Balaam?

days.title: Sin at Peor
days.intro: At Peor, Israelite men are drawn into immorality and the worship of Baal by Moabite women, and a plague breaks out until Phinehas acts in zeal. A new census follows on the plains of Moab. Of those counted at Sinai, only Caleb and Joshua remain.
days.question: What small compromise could lead you away from God if left unchecked?

days.title: Joshua Is Chosen
days.intro: The daughters of Zelophehad ask for their father’s inheritance, and God agrees. Moses sees the promised land from a mountain and asks for a shepherd for the people, and Joshua is commissioned by the laying on of hands. Then come the offerings for each day, sabbath and feast.
days.question: Who has God given you to guide, and who is guiding you?

days.title: Vows and War with Midian
days.intro: Laws on vows explain when a father or husband may cancel a woman’s vow. Then Israel goes to war against Midian for leading the people into sin at Peor. Balaam is killed among the Midianites, and the spoils are divided, with a share set aside for the Lord.
days.question: How seriously do you take the promises you make to God and others?

days.title: Settling East of the Jordan
days.intro: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh want to settle the good grazing land east of the Jordan. Moses fears they are abandoning their brothers, but they promise to fight alongside them first. Then comes a list of every stage of Israel’s journey from Egypt.
days.question: Looking back over your own journey, where do you see God’s guidance?

days.title: Cities of Refuge
days.intro: God sets the borders of Canaan and names the leaders who will divide it. The Levites receive towns, six of them cities of refuge where someone who killed without intent may flee. Numbers ends with the daughters of Zelophehad marrying within their tribe to keep the inheritance.
days.question: Who needs you to be a place of refuge for them right now?

days.title: Moses Remembers the Journey
days.intro: On the plains of Moab, Moses begins his farewell speeches. He recalls choosing judges, sending the spies and the people’s refusal to enter the land. He reviews the long wandering, God’s order to pass Edom, Moab and Ammon in peace, and the victory over Sihon.
days.question: What lesson from your own past do you most need to remember?

days.title: A God So Near
days.intro: Moses recalls defeating Og and settling the land east of the Jordan. He may see Canaan but not enter it. He urges Israel to keep the commandments and shun idols, since at Horeb they saw no form, only heard a voice. Whoever seeks God wholeheartedly will find him.
days.question: How near does God feel to you today, and why?

days.title: Hear, O Israel
days.intro: Moses repeats the Ten Commandments given at Horeb. Then comes the great command: love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul and strength, and teach these words to your children. God chose Israel not because they were many, but because he loved them.
days.question: How are you passing on your love of God to those around you?

days.title: Not by Bread Alone
days.intro: Moses reminds Israel that God fed them with manna to teach that man does not live by bread alone. He warns them not to forget God when they prosper, nor to think they earned the land. Recalling the golden calf, he asks them to love God and circumcise their hearts.
days.question: When life is comfortable, how do you keep from forgetting God?

days.title: One Place of Worship
days.intro: Israel must destroy the shrines of other gods and bring sacrifices only to the place God will choose. False prophets and anyone urging idolatry must not be followed, even if their signs come true. Rules on clean food follow, and tithes that feed the Levite, stranger, orphan and widow.
days.question: What voices pull you away from God, even when they sound convincing?

days.title: A Prophet Like Moses
days.intro: Every seventh year debts are released, and Israel must open its hand to the poor. The great feasts are repeated, judges must be fair, and a future king must copy and study God’s law. Moses forbids fortune-telling and promises that God will raise up a prophet like him.
days.question: Where could you open your hand more generously to someone in need?

days.title: Justice in the Land
days.intro: Moses keeps laying out how Israel should live once settled. Cities of refuge protect someone who kills by accident. Then come rules for honest witnesses, warfare, unsolved murders and family life, plus everyday kindness: bring back a neighbor’s stray ox, and put a railing around your roof.
days.question: Whose safety or belongings could you look out for this week, as Moses asks Israel to?

days.title: Firstfruits and Fair Dealing
days.intro: More laws touch daily life: pay a poor worker before sunset, leave gleanings for the widow, orphan and stranger, and keep honest weights. In chapter 26 the farmer brings his firstfruits and recalls aloud how God led Israel out of Egypt into a land flowing with milk and honey.
days.question: What firstfruits of your time or money could you give God first, rather than last?

days.title: Blessings and Curses
days.intro: Moses tells Israel to write the law on plastered stones once they cross the Jordan, and to proclaim blessings and curses from Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. Chapter 28 spells out both at length: abundance for faithfulness, and frightening ruin, even exile, for turning away.
days.question: Which of God’s commands do you find hardest to see as a blessing rather than a burden?

days.title: Choose Life
days.intro: The covenant is renewed in the land of Moab. God promises mercy to those who return to him, even from exile, and says his command is not far off but very near. Then comes the great choice: life or death. Moses, now 120, hands leadership to Joshua.
days.question: What small choice today could be your way of choosing life?

days.title: The Death of Moses
days.intro: Moses sings a long song recalling God’s faithfulness and Israel’s fickleness, then blesses each tribe in turn. From Mount Nebo he sees the whole promised land he will not enter. He dies there, the Lord buries him, and no prophet like Moses arises again.
days.question: How do you respond when you work toward something you may not live to see finished?

days.title: Crossing the Jordan
days.intro: God tells Joshua again and again to be strong and take courage. Rahab hides two spies in Jericho and asks for mercy. The priests carry the ark into the Jordan, its waters stop, and Israel crosses on dry ground. At Gilgal they keep the Passover, and the manna ends.
days.question: Where is God asking you to step forward before the way ahead looks clear?

days.title: The Walls of Jericho
days.intro: Israel marches around Jericho for seven days, and the walls fall at the trumpet blast and the people’s shout. Rahab and her family are spared. Then one man’s hidden theft brings defeat at Ai, until Achan is found out. Ai is taken, and the law is read aloud.
days.question: Is there something hidden in your life that weighs on others more than you realize?

days.title: The Sun Stands Still
days.intro: The Gibeonites trick Israel with worn-out shoes and dry, crumbling bread, and Joshua makes a treaty without consulting the Lord. When five kings attack Gibeon, Joshua defends it: hailstones fall, and at his prayer the sun and moon stand still. The northern kings fall next.
days.question: What decision are you facing that you have not yet brought to God in prayer?

days.title: Caleb Claims Hebron
days.intro: Chapter 12 lists the kings defeated under Moses and Joshua. God then tells the aging Joshua to divide the land, starting with the tribes east of the Jordan, while Levi receives no land of its own. Caleb, now 85 and still strong, asks for Hebron.
days.question: What promise of God are you still waiting on, like Caleb, after many years?

days.title: Judah and Joseph’s Lands
days.intro: The borders and towns of Judah fill chapter 15, with a lively scene: Caleb’s daughter asks her father for springs of water. Then come the lands of Ephraim and Manasseh. Zelophehad’s daughters receive their promised share, and Joseph’s sons are told to clear the forest.
days.question: What do you need to ask God for plainly, the way Caleb’s daughter asked her father?

days.title: Shiloh and Cities of Refuge
days.intro: The tabernacle is set up at Shiloh. Seven tribes still lack land, so Joshua sends men to map it and casts lots before the Lord. Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun and the rest receive their portions, Joshua receives his town last, and six cities of refuge are named.
days.question: Who could find refuge with you after making a mistake?

days.title: Not One Promise Failed
days.intro: The Levites receive towns scattered among all the tribes, and the narrator pauses: not one of God’s promises failed. The eastern tribes go home and build a large altar by the Jordan, nearly starting a war until they explain it. Old Joshua urges Israel to stay faithful.
days.question: Looking back, which of God’s promises have you seen come true in your own life?

days.title: As for Me and My House
days.intro: At Shechem Joshua retells Israel’s story and puts the choice before them: he and his house will serve the Lord. The people agree, and Joshua dies. Judges then shows tribes leaving Canaanites in place, and a pattern begins: sin, oppression, crying out, rescue.
days.question: What would it look like for your household to choose, together, to serve the Lord?

days.title: Ehud, Deborah and Jael
days.intro: The cycle turns again and again. Othniel rescues Israel, Ehud kills Eglon king of Moab with a hidden sword, and Shamgar fights with a plowshare. The prophetess Deborah sends Barak into battle, but Jael, a woman in a tent, strikes down the enemy general Sisera. Deborah sings of victory.
days.question: When have you been surprised by whom God chose to use?

days.title: Gideon and the Three Hundred
days.intro: An angel finds Gideon threshing wheat in hiding and calls him most valiant. Hesitant, Gideon asks for signs with a fleece. God trims his army to three hundred, who rout Midian with trumpets, jars and lamps. Gideon refuses a crown, yet the ephod he makes becomes a snare.
days.question: Where do you feel too small for what God asks, as Gideon did?

days.title: Abimelech’s Grab for Power
days.intro: Gideon’s son Abimelech murders his seventy brothers to rule Shechem. The one survivor, Jotham, tells a parable of trees choosing a bramble for king. Betrayal turns to bloodshed until a woman drops a millstone on Abimelech. Israel strays again, then repents, and God is moved by their misery.
days.question: Where are you tempted to grab for control instead of waiting on God?

days.title: Jephthah’s Vow, Samson’s Birth
days.intro: Jephthah, an outcast, leads Gilead against Ammon and makes a rash vow that costs him his only daughter. A bitter fight with Ephraim follows. Then an angel announces Samson’s birth to a childless woman. Samson grows strong, kills a lion, and poses a riddle at his wedding.
days.question: Have you ever made a hasty promise? What did it teach you about speaking carefully?

days.title: Samson and Delilah
days.intro: Samson’s feud with the Philistines escalates: burned fields, a jawbone, a thousand dead. Delilah pries out the secret of his strength, and he is blinded and chained. In the temple of Dagon he prays once more. Then Micah sets up an idol, and the tribe of Dan steals it.
days.question: What weakness do you keep returning to, even when you know where it leads?

days.title: Israel Without a King
days.intro: A dark ending. A Levite’s wife is abused and killed at Gibeah in Benjamin, and the tribes go to war. Benjamin is nearly wiped out, and Israel scrambles to find wives for the survivors. The book’s refrain sums it up: everyone did what seemed right to himself.
days.question: Who helps you see what is truly right, not just what seems right to you?

days.title: Ruth’s Faithful Love
days.intro: Naomi loses her husband and sons in Moab and returns home bitter. Her daughter-in-law Ruth refuses to leave her: your people will be my people, and your God my God. Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz, who marries her. Their son Obed is David’s grandfather.
days.question: Who has stayed loyal to you in hard times, and how can you thank them?

days.title: Hannah’s Prayer, Samuel’s Call
days.intro: Childless Hannah pours out her heart at Shiloh, and God gives her Samuel, whom she gives back to serve him. Her song praises a God who lifts up the lowly. Eli’s sons are corrupt. The boy Samuel hears God calling at night. Then the Philistines capture the ark.
days.question: How could you make a little quiet today to hear what God may be saying?

days.title: The People Want a King
days.intro: The captured ark topples the idol Dagon and brings plagues, so the Philistines send it back on a cart. Samuel leads Israel to put away idols and win victory. When his sons prove unjust, the people demand a king. Then Saul, looking for lost donkeys, meets Samuel.
days.question: Where are you tempted to want to be just like everyone else around you?

days.title: Saul Becomes King
days.intro: Samuel anoints Saul, who is given another heart and prophesies. Chosen by lot, he is found hiding at home. He rescues Jabesh-gilead from the Ammonites, and Samuel warns the people to stay faithful. But facing the Philistines, Saul grows impatient and offers sacrifice without waiting for Samuel.
days.question: When waiting on God feels too slow, what do you tend to do instead?

days.title: Obedience Over Sacrifice
days.intro: Jonathan and his armor-bearer climb a cliff and set the Philistines running. Saul’s rash oath nearly costs Jonathan his life. Sent against Amalek, Saul spares King Agag and the best livestock. Samuel tells him that obedience is better than sacrifice, and the Lord rejects Saul as king.
days.question: Is there a partial obedience in your life that you call good enough?

days.title: David and Goliath
days.intro: Samuel goes to Bethlehem and anoints Jesse’s youngest son, the shepherd David, because the Lord looks at the heart. David soothes Saul with his harp. Then the giant Goliath taunts Israel, and David faces him with a sling and five smooth stones, trusting in the Lord.
days.question: What giant are you facing, and what would trusting God with it look like?

days.title: Jonathan’s Friendship
days.intro: Jonathan loves David as his own soul and makes a covenant with him. As women sing David’s praises, Saul’s jealousy turns murderous: a thrown spear, a trap through marriage to Michal, soldiers at the door. Jonathan warns David with arrows shot in a field, and they part in tears.
days.question: Who is a friend who helps you stay close to God, and how can you be one?

days.title: David Spares Saul
days.intro: On the run, David receives holy bread from Ahimelech and pretends to be mad before a Philistine king. Saul has the priests of Nob slaughtered. In a cave at En-gedi, David could kill Saul but only cuts the hem of his robe, refusing to harm the Lord’s anointed.
days.question: When someone wrongs you, what would it look like to leave justice to God?

days.title: Abigail’s Wise Words
days.intro: Samuel dies. When the rich fool Nabal insults David’s men, David sets out for revenge, but Nabal’s wife Abigail meets him with gifts and wise words, and David thanks God for stopping him. Again he spares the sleeping Saul, then takes refuge among the Philistines.
days.question: Who has talked you out of a decision you would have regretted?

days.title: Saul’s Last Battle
days.intro: With God silent, a desperate Saul consults a medium at Endor, and Samuel foretells his death. The Philistine commanders send David away. Raiders burn Ziklag, but David takes courage in the Lord and recovers everything. On Mount Gilboa, Saul and his sons fall.
days.question: When God seems silent, where do you turn first?

days.title: David Mourns Saul and Jonathan
days.intro: David grieves for Saul and Jonathan in a moving lament: how are the valiant fallen. Judah anoints him king at Hebron, while Saul’s son Ish-bosheth rules the rest of Israel. A long war follows. Abner, Saul’s general, comes over to David, but Joab murders him, and David mourns openly.
days.question: How do you grieve someone who hurt you, yet whom you also loved?

days.title: A House Forever
days.intro: David becomes king over all Israel, takes Jerusalem, and brings up the ark, dancing before the Lord with all his might. When he wants to build God a house, Nathan brings a greater promise: God will build David a house, and his throne will stand forever.
days.question: What would it look like to worship God with your whole self, without worrying who is watching?

days.title: David and Bathsheba
days.intro: David shows kindness to Jonathan’s lame son Mephibosheth. Then, staying home from war, he takes Bathsheba and arranges her husband Uriah’s death to hide it. Nathan tells a story about a poor man’s lamb and says: you are the man. David confesses and is forgiven, yet suffers the consequences.
days.question: Is there a sin you have explained away that you need to name honestly, as David did?

days.title: Absalom’s Rebellion
days.intro: Trouble grows inside David’s family. Amnon violates his half-sister Tamar, and her brother Absalom kills him and flees. Brought back, Absalom wins the people’s hearts at the city gate and declares himself king. David leaves Jerusalem barefoot, weeping as he climbs the Mount of Olives.
days.question: Where does a rift in your family need attention before it grows worse?

days.title: O My Son Absalom
days.intro: As David flees, Shimei curses him and throws stones, and David lets him be. Ahithophel gives Absalom shrewd advice, but David’s friend Hushai undoes it. In the forest battle Absalom is caught in a tree and killed by Joab. David weeps, wishing he had died instead.
days.question: How do you respond when someone criticizes you unfairly, as Shimei did David?

days.title: The King Returns
days.intro: Joab shakes David out of his grief. On the way back to Jerusalem, David pardons Shimei, hears out Mephibosheth, and honors old Barzillai. Tribal rivalry flares into Sheba’s revolt, which a wise woman ends. A famine is traced to Saul’s wrong against the Gibeonites.
days.question: Whom do you need to forgive or welcome back for a fresh start?

days.title: The Lord Is My Rock
days.intro: David sings his thanks for rescue from all his enemies; the song closely matches Psalm 17 (18). Then come his last words about a just ruler, and a roll of his mighty warriors, including three who risked their lives to bring him water from the well at Bethlehem.
days.question: Which rescue in your life would you put in your own song of thanks?

days.title: David’s Census, Adam’s Line
days.intro: David orders a count of his fighting men and then sees his sin. A plague follows, stopped when he builds an altar on Araunah’s threshing floor, refusing to offer God what costs him nothing. First Chronicles then begins, tracing the human family from Adam to Abraham and Esau.
days.question: What would it mean to give God something that truly costs you?

days.title: The Line of Judah and David
days.intro: Chronicles begins its retelling of Israel’s story with names. Today’s lists trace the tribe of Judah down to Jesse and David, then David’s sons and the royal line of kings that followed, on past the exile. These names point toward Jesus, the Son of David.
days.question: Whose faith in your family helped pass the faith on to you?

days.title: The Prayer of Jabez
days.intro: More family lists, from Judah, Simeon and the tribes east of the Jordan. Watch for Jabez, more honored than his brothers, who asks God for blessing and protection and receives it. The eastern tribes win when they call on God in battle, but later turn to idols and are exiled.
days.question: What would you ask God for today if you prayed as boldly as Jabez?

days.title: The Tribe of Levi
days.intro: One long chapter on Levi, the priestly tribe: the high priests descended from Aaron, the Levite families, and the singers David put in charge of music before the ark, such as Heman and Asaph. It closes with the towns given to the Levites throughout Israel.
days.question: How does music or song help you pray?

days.title: Families of the Tribes
days.intro: The lists continue with Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher, often counting their warriors; Joshua appears among Ephraim’s descendants. Chapter 8 traces Benjamin again, down to Saul and his family. Names that seem dry still witness that God remembers every family.
days.question: When did you last sense that God knows you by name?

days.title: David Takes Zion
days.intro: Chapter 9 lists those who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, including gatekeepers who guarded the house of God. Chronicles then tells Saul’s death briefly, naming his unfaithfulness as the cause. All Israel makes David king, he captures the fortress of Zion, and his mighty men are listed.
days.question: What small unfaithfulness might be quietly shaping the direction of your life?

days.title: The Ark Comes to Jerusalem
days.intro: Warriors from every tribe rally to David, including men of Issachar who understood the times. The first attempt to move the ark ends with Uzzah’s death. After three months with Obed-edom, the Levites carry it properly, and David leads the celebration with music and dancing.
days.question: What would it mean for you to understand the times and know what to do?

days.title: David’s Song of Thanks
days.intro: With the ark in its tent, David appoints Levites to praise God and gives them a song of thanks that echoes several Psalms. Nathan then brings God’s promise that David’s son will build a house and that his kingdom will last forever. Victories over neighboring nations follow.
days.question: What is one thing you could thank God for out loud today?

days.title: Preparing for the Temple
days.intro: After the census and plague, David buys Ornan’s threshing floor and names it the site of God’s house. Barred from building because he shed much blood, he gathers materials, charges young Solomon to build, and organizes the Levites. Today’s Psalm prays for the king’s son.
days.question: What could you prepare now so that someone after you can build something good?

days.title: Priests, Singers, Gatekeepers
days.intro: David organizes temple service. The priests are divided by lot into twenty-four groups; the eighth, Abijah, is the group Zechariah belongs to in Luke’s Gospel. Singers are set apart to prophesy with harps and cymbals, and gatekeepers and treasurers receive their posts.
days.question: What small, steady service could you offer your parish?

days.title: David’s Last Gifts
days.intro: After lists of army divisions and officials, David gathers the leaders and hands Solomon the plans for the temple. He gives generously from his own treasure, and the people gladly follow. His prayer confesses that everything comes from God’s hand. Then David dies, full of days.
days.question: What would change if you saw everything you own as received from God’s hand?

days.title: Solomon Takes the Throne
days.intro: As David grows old, his son Adonijah declares himself king. Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his promise, and Solomon is anointed. David charges Solomon to walk in God’s ways, then dies. Solomon secures his throne, removing Adonijah, Joab and Shimei.
days.question: What charge would you want to hand on to those who come after you?

days.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
days.intro: At Gibeon God invites Solomon to ask for anything, and he asks for an understanding heart to judge the people. God gives him wisdom, and riches and honor besides. Two women claim one baby, and Solomon’s ruling reveals the true mother. Hiram of Tyre agrees to supply cedar.
days.question: If God offered you anything, what would you ask for, and why?

days.title: Building the Temple
days.intro: Detail after detail: the temple’s size, its cedar and gold, the inner sanctuary with two great cherubim. The stones were readied beforehand, so no hammer or axe was heard as it rose. Solomon’s palace follows, then the bronze pillars and the great basin called the sea.
days.question: How do you prepare your heart before entering a church?

days.title: The Glory Fills the Temple
days.intro: The ark is brought in, and a cloud fills the house of the Lord. Solomon prays: heaven cannot contain God, much less this temple, yet may he hear every prayer made toward it, even a foreigner’s. God answers with a promise and a warning against turning away.
days.question: Where do you most sense God’s presence close to you?

days.title: Solomon’s Heart Turns
days.intro: The Queen of Sheba tests Solomon with hard questions and leaves amazed. His wealth is staggering. But in old age his many foreign wives turn his heart to their gods. God raises up enemies, and the prophet Ahijah tears a new cloak to promise Jeroboam ten tribes.
days.question: What good gift in your life could slowly pull your heart away from God?

days.title: The Temple on Moriah
days.intro: Chronicles retells Solomon’s reign with the temple at its center. He builds on Mount Moriah, where the Lord had appeared to David. When the ark is placed inside and the singers praise God’s everlasting mercy, a cloud fills the house. Today’s Psalm celebrates God dwelling in Zion.
days.question: When has praising God with others made him feel especially near?

days.title: I Will Heal Their Land
days.intro: Solomon prays at the temple’s dedication, and fire falls from heaven on the sacrifices. God appears at night with a promise: if his people pray, seek his face, and turn from their wicked ways, he will hear, forgive their sins and heal their land. Solomon’s building projects follow.
days.question: What turning from sin would most help heal your home or community?

days.title: The Song of Songs Begins
days.intro: Chronicles closes Solomon’s story with the Queen of Sheba’s visit and his death. Then the Song of Songs begins, a love poem between bride and bridegroom. The Church has long read it as a picture of God’s love for his people and for each soul. Listen for longing and delight.
days.question: How might your prayer change if you believed God truly delights in you?

days.title: Love Strong as Death
days.intro: The Song ends with the bride searching for her beloved and declaring that love is strong as death; many waters cannot quench it. Then Ecclesiastes opens with a sigh: vanity of vanities. Its writer tries pleasure, great works and wealth, and finds them empty.
days.question: What have you chased hoping it would satisfy you, only to find it empty?

days.title: A Time for Everything
days.intro: Ecclesiastes keeps looking honestly at life under the sun. There is a time to be born and a time to die. Two are better than one. Let your words before God be few, and keep your vows. The lover of money is never satisfied.
days.question: What season of life are you in, and what might God be asking of you in it?

days.title: Remember Your Creator
days.intro: Ecclesiastes admits we cannot fully grasp God’s ways, but urges us to eat our bread with joy, do earnestly whatever our hands can do, and give generously while there is time. It ends by calling us to remember our Creator in youth, to fear God and keep his commandments.
days.question: What good work could you do today rather than putting it off?

days.title: The Kingdom Splits
days.intro: Rehoboam ignores his elders and promises a heavier yoke, so ten tribes break away under Jeroboam. To keep his people from going to Jerusalem, Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan. A man of God from Judah confronts him, and Egypt’s king plunders the temple.
days.question: Whose wise advice have you brushed aside because it was not what you wanted?

days.title: Elijah and the Widow
days.intro: Kings come and go quickly. Asa of Judah does right, while Israel’s throne passes through plots and murders to Omri and his son Ahab, who serves Baal with his wife Jezebel. Then the prophet Elijah announces a drought, is fed by ravens, and raises a widow’s son.
days.question: When have you given from very little, like the widow, and found God provided?

days.title: Fire on Mount Carmel
days.intro: On Mount Carmel Elijah asks the people how long they will waver between two sides, and faces the prophets of Baal. Fire falls from heaven, then rain. Yet threatened by Jezebel, he flees in despair. An angel feeds him, and at Horeb the Lord comes in a gentle breeze.
days.question: Where might God be speaking to you quietly while you wait for something louder?

days.title: Naboth’s Vineyard
days.intro: Ahab wants Naboth’s vineyard, and when Naboth will not sell his family inheritance, Jezebel has him falsely accused and stoned. Elijah pronounces judgment, and Ahab humbles himself. Later the prophet Micaiah alone tells Ahab the truth, and Ahab dies in battle despite his disguise.
days.question: Is there a truth you avoid hearing because it might ask something of you?

days.title: Elijah Taken Up
days.intro: King Ahaziah sends to consult a foreign god, and Elijah foretells his death. Then Elijah crosses the Jordan with Elisha and is taken up by a whirlwind as a chariot of fire appears. Elisha receives a double share of his spirit and begins his own works.
days.question: Whose faith would you most like to inherit, and why?

days.title: Naaman Is Healed
days.intro: Elisha’s miracles meet ordinary needs: a widow’s oil keeps flowing, a generous woman receives a son and later sees him raised, and a little bread feeds a hundred men. Naaman, a Syrian general, grudgingly washes seven times in the Jordan and is healed, while greedy Gehazi is struck with leprosy.
days.question: Where does pride keep you from accepting a simple remedy God offers?

days.title: Chariots of Fire Around Elisha
days.intro: An axe head floats. When Syrian troops surround Elisha, his frightened servant’s eyes are opened to see the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire. Later Samaria starves under siege, until four lepers find the enemy camp deserted. Elisha foresees Hazael’s cruelty.
days.question: What would change if you could see God’s help around you right now?

days.title: Jehu and Queen Athaliah
days.intro: A young prophet anoints Jehu, who drives furiously to wipe out Ahab’s house: two kings and Jezebel die. He destroys Baal worship but keeps Jeroboam’s calves. In Judah, Athaliah seizes power, but the boy Joash is hidden in the temple for six years and then crowned.
days.question: Where are you zealous against others’ faults but easy on your own?

days.title: Jonah Runs Away
days.intro: Joash repairs the temple. Elisha dies, and a dead man who touches his bones comes back to life. Under Jeroboam II, a word spoken by the prophet Jonah son of Amittai comes true. Then the Book of Jonah begins: sent to Nineveh, Jonah sails the other way.
days.question: Where are you heading the other way from something God has asked of you?

days.title: Nineveh Repents
days.intro: From inside the fish Jonah prays, and he is cast out onto dry land. He preaches, and all Nineveh repents. Jonah sulks, and God shows him his care for the city. Amos then opens with judgments on Israel’s neighbors, and on Israel for selling the poor.
days.question: Is there someone you find it hard to wish God’s mercy for?

days.title: Seek the Lord and Live
days.intro: Amos calls Israel to seek the Lord and live. God rejects their feasts while justice is trampled. Amos sees visions of coming judgment and is told to leave Bethel. Yet the book ends with hope: David’s fallen tabernacle will rise. Today’s Psalm also calls rulers to defend the poor.
days.question: Where could your faith show itself in fairness toward someone poor or overlooked?

days.title: Hosea’s Unfaithful Wife
days.intro: God tells Hosea to marry Gomer, an unfaithful wife, as a living sign of Israel’s unfaithfulness to the Lord. Their children’s names announce judgment. Yet God promises to lead his people into the wilderness and speak to their heart, and says he desires mercy, not sacrifice.
days.question: How has God kept loving you through times when you were unfaithful?

days.title: Drawn with Bands of Love
days.intro: Hosea grieves over Israel’s idols and empty alliances: they sow the wind and reap a whirlwind. Then God speaks like a parent: he called his son out of Egypt, carried him in his arms, and drew him with bands of love. He will not destroy him utterly.
days.question: How have you felt God’s patient, fatherly love drawing you back?

days.title: Return to the Lord
days.intro: Hosea ends with judgment and hope: God will redeem his people from death itself, and he pleads, return, O Israel, promising to heal them. Back in Kings, Israel’s rulers are murdered one after another, and Judah’s King Ahaz copies a pagan altar for the temple.
days.question: What would returning to the Lord look like for you this week?

days.title: Israel Exiled, Tobit Faithful
days.intro: Samaria falls to Assyria, and the northern tribes are carried into exile because they abandoned the Lord. Newcomers mix his worship with their own gods. Then we meet Tobit, an exile in Nineveh who stays faithful, gives alms and buries the dead, until he is suddenly blinded.
days.question: How could you practice mercy quietly, as Tobit did, even when it costs you?

days.title: Two Prayers Heard at Once
days.intro: On the same day, blind Tobit and Sarah, a young woman in Media who has lost seven husbands, pour out their grief to God. God hears both and sends the angel Raphael. Tobit gives his son Tobiah wise counsel, and a stranger offers to guide him.
days.question: When have you brought your deepest discouragement honestly to God in prayer?

days.title: Tobiah and Sarah Marry
days.intro: Guided by Raphael, Tobiah catches a fish that leaps at him and keeps its heart, liver and gall. At Raguel’s house he marries Sarah, and the two pray together on their wedding night. Back home, his mother Anna fears he is lost.
days.question: How could prayer shape your closest relationships more deeply?

days.title: Raphael Reveals Himself
days.intro: Tobiah comes home and heals his father’s eyes with the fish’s gall. Raphael then reveals who he is: one of the seven who stand before the Lord, who brought their prayers to God. Tobit sings God’s praise and, before dying, urges his family to stay faithful.
days.question: Looking back, where can you see God guiding you when you did not recognize it?

days.title: Do Justice, Love Mercy
days.intro: Micah condemns the rich who seize fields, prophets who preach for pay, and judges who take bribes. Yet he sees nations streaming to God’s mountain and a ruler coming from little Bethlehem. In chapter 6, God says plainly what he asks of us.
days.question: Which of Micah’s three requests, justice, mercy, or humility, is hardest for you right now?

days.title: Scarlet Sins Made White
days.intro: Isaiah opens with God’s case against Judah: sacrifices offered while widows and orphans are neglected. Yet God offers to make scarlet sins white as snow. In chapter 2 the nations go up to the Lord’s house and beat their swords into plowshares.
days.question: Which injustice near you is God asking you to help set right?

days.title: Isaiah’s Call and Emmanuel
days.intro: A love song about a vineyard turns into judgment. In chapter 6 Isaiah sees the Lord enthroned, seraphim cry “Holy,” and a burning coal cleanses his lips. Then he offers King Ahaz a sign: a virgin will bear a son named Emmanuel.
days.question: When you sense God asking, “Whom shall I send?”, how do you usually answer?

days.title: A Child Is Born to Us
days.intro: Light breaks on a people in darkness: a child is born, the Prince of Peace, to reign on David’s throne. Assyria is God’s rod but will fall for its pride. From the root of Jesse a shoot rises, filled with the Spirit, and the wolf lies down with the lamb.
days.question: Where do you most long for the peace this promised King brings?

days.title: Babylon’s Pride Brought Low
days.intro: Isaiah now speaks to Judah’s neighbors: Babylon, Philistia, Moab, Damascus. At the center is a taunt over Babylon’s king, who wanted to climb above the stars and fell instead. Through it all the message holds steady: no empire can stand against the Lord.
days.question: What ambitions in your life quietly try to climb above God?

days.title: The Key of David
days.intro: The oracles continue against Ethiopia, Egypt, Babylon, Edom and Arabia. Isaiah walks barefoot for three years as a sign. Surprisingly, Egypt will one day know the Lord. In chapter 22 the steward Shebna is replaced by Eliakim, who receives the key of David’s house.
days.question: What responsibility has God placed on your shoulder, and how are you carrying it?

days.title: A Feast on the Mountain
days.intro: After an oracle on proud Tyre, the view widens to the whole earth under judgment. Then great hope breaks in: a rich banquet on God’s mountain for all peoples, death destroyed forever, tears wiped from every face, and songs of trust in God.
days.question: Whose tears do you long to see God wipe away?

days.title: Trusting God, Not Egypt
days.intro: Isaiah rebukes leaders drunk on wine and on false confidence. God lays a tested cornerstone in Zion. The people honor him with their lips while their hearts are far away, and they run to Egypt for help instead of returning to him in quiet trust.
days.question: Where are you tempted to seek security apart from God?

days.title: The Desert Will Bloom
days.intro: Again Isaiah warns against leaning on Egypt’s horses. He pictures a king who reigns in justice, and judgment falling on God’s enemies. The day ends in joy: the desert blossoms, the blind see, the lame leap, and a holy way leads the redeemed home.
days.question: What dry place in your life needs God’s renewing water?

days.title: Hezekiah’s Crisis and Prayer
days.intro: Assyria’s King Sennacherib threatens Jerusalem, and his officer mocks Judah’s God. Hezekiah spreads the enemy’s letter before the Lord, and the Assyrian army is struck down. Later, gravely ill, Hezekiah weeps and is given fifteen more years, then foolishly shows his treasures to Babylon’s envoys.
days.question: What threatening situation could you lay before the Lord today, as Hezekiah did?

days.title: Jerusalem Delivered
days.intro: These chapters tell Hezekiah’s story again, much as Isaiah did. Notice what is new: Hezekiah smashes the bronze serpent Moses made, because people were burning incense to it. Then come Sennacherib’s threats, the night of deliverance, the healing, and the warning about Babylon.
days.question: Has something good in your life quietly become an idol?

days.title: Josiah Finds the Law
days.intro: Manasseh undoes his father’s reforms, filling Judah with idols and innocent blood. His grandson Josiah repairs the temple, where the book of the law is found. Josiah tears his garments, reads it to the people, renews the covenant, and clears idolatry from the land.
days.question: What part of God’s word has recently cut you to the heart?

days.title: Jerusalem Falls
days.intro: Babylon carries King Jehoiachin away, then returns when Zedekiah rebels. The city and temple are burned and the people exiled. Chronicles then takes us back to the kingdom’s split under Rehoboam, retelling Judah’s story with special attention to the temple and its worship.
days.question: When everything familiar falls apart, what keeps you anchored to God?

days.title: Asa Seeks the Lord
days.intro: Rehoboam abandons the law, and Egypt’s king plunders the temple. Abijah defeats Jeroboam by relying on God. King Asa begins well, removing idols and renewing the covenant after a prophet’s word. Late in life, though, he leans on Syria instead of God and turns harsh.
days.question: How do you keep a good beginning with God from fading over time?

days.title: The Battle Is God’s
days.intro: Jehoshaphat sends teachers of the law through Judah and appoints honest judges. His alliance with Ahab nearly costs him his life. When a vast army comes, he leads the people in fasting and prayer, and singers march ahead of the troops. The enemies destroy one another.
days.question: What battle are you fighting alone that you could hand over to God?

days.title: Joash and Jehoiada
days.intro: Jehoram and Ahaziah follow Ahab’s ways. Queen Athaliah seizes power, but a hidden child, Joash, survives. The priest Jehoiada crowns him, and Joash repairs the temple. After Jehoiada dies, Joash turns to idols and has the priest’s son Zechariah stoned.
days.question: Who helps keep you faithful, and how would you stand without them?

days.title: Pride Before a Fall
days.intro: Amaziah starts well but ends badly. Uzziah grows strong, then proudly burns incense in the temple, a priest’s task, and is struck with leprosy. Jotham reigns faithfully. Ahaz sinks into idolatry, yet watch the prophet Oded persuade Israel’s army to free and care for Judah’s captives.
days.question: When success comes, how do you guard against the pride that undid Uzziah?

days.title: Hezekiah Restores Worship
days.intro: Hezekiah reopens and cleanses the temple and restores its sacrifices. He invites all Israel, even the northern tribes, to keep the Passover in Jerusalem. The joy is so great that the feast runs a second week, and the people give generously for the priests and Levites.
days.question: Is there a neglected place of prayer in your life that needs reopening?

days.title: Manasseh Repents
days.intro: Sennacherib’s invasion is retold briefly. Then comes something only Chronicles records: the wicked Manasseh, taken in chains to Babylon, humbles himself and prays. God hears him and brings him home, and he removes the idols. Later his grandson Josiah renews the covenant.
days.question: Whom have you written off as beyond the reach of God’s mercy?

days.title: Exile and Nineveh’s Fall
days.intro: Josiah keeps a great Passover but dies in battle against Egypt’s king, and Jeremiah mourns him. Judah’s last kings fail and the people go into exile, yet Chronicles ends with Cyrus allowing a return. Nahum then announces the fall of Nineveh, Assyria’s proud capital.
days.question: How does the hopeful ending of Chronicles speak to a loss you carry?

days.title: The Just Shall Live by Faith
days.intro: Zephaniah warns of the day of the Lord, then promises a humble remnant and a God who rejoices over his people with song. Habakkuk asks why God lets evil go unchecked. God answers that the vision will surely come, and the just one lives by faith.
days.question: What question would you bring to God as boldly as Habakkuk did?

days.title: Jeremiah Is Called
days.intro: Habakkuk ends with a prayer: even if the fig tree fails and the fields yield nothing, he will rejoice in God. Then young Jeremiah is called, known by God before his birth. God accuses his people of leaving the fountain of living water for broken cisterns.
days.question: What broken cistern do you sometimes drink from instead of God?

days.title: Return, Faithless Children
days.intro: God pictures Israel and Judah as an unfaithful wife, yet still pleads with them to come home and promises shepherds after his own heart. He asks for circumcised hearts, not just outward signs. Jeremiah searches Jerusalem’s streets for even one person who acts justly.
days.question: What would returning to God with your whole heart look like this week?

days.title: The Temple Sermon
days.intro: False prophets cry peace when there is no peace. At the temple gate Jeremiah warns that the building will not protect people who steal, kill, and serve idols, then claim safety inside. God urges them to seek the ancient paths, and the prophet grieves over their refusal.
days.question: Where might you be relying on religious habits without a changed heart?

days.title: A Prophet Who Weeps
days.intro: Jeremiah wishes his eyes were a fountain of tears for his people. God says to boast only in knowing him. Idols cannot speak or walk, but the Lord made the earth. Men from Jeremiah’s own town plot to kill him, and he asks God why the wicked prosper.
days.question: When have you asked God why the wicked seem to prosper?

days.title: The Ruined Loincloth
days.intro: Jeremiah hides a linen loincloth by the Euphrates and later finds it ruined, a sign of Judah’s pride. Drought strikes and he pleads for his people, but God refuses. Jeremiah complains bitterly, yet finds joy in God’s words. He is told not to marry, a sign of coming loss.
days.question: When have God’s words tasted sweet to you, and why?

days.title: At the Potter’s House
days.intro: Whoever trusts in human strength is like a desert shrub; whoever trusts in God is a tree by water. At the potter’s house Jeremiah learns that God can reshape his people. After smashing a clay jar as a sign, he is beaten and put in the stocks.
days.question: What would it mean to let God reshape you like clay right now?

days.title: The Righteous Branch
days.intro: As Babylon besieges Jerusalem, King Zedekiah hopes for a miracle, but Jeremiah tells him the city will fall. He judges kings who built palaces through injustice. God condemns shepherds who scatter the flock and promises a righteous Branch from David who will reign wisely.
days.question: Whom has God given you to shepherd, and how are you caring for them?

days.title: Good Figs and Bad
days.intro: Two baskets of figs show God’s care for the exiles already in Babylon. Jeremiah foretells seventy years of captivity. When he warns of the temple’s ruin, priests demand his death, but officials spare him. He then wears yoke straps to show the nations must serve Babylon.
days.question: How do you respond when someone speaks a hard truth to you?

days.title: Seek the City’s Peace
days.intro: The prophet Hananiah breaks Jeremiah’s yoke and promises a quick return, but dies within the year. Jeremiah writes to the exiles: build houses, plant gardens, and pray for Babylon’s peace. After seventy years God will bring them home. Chapter 30 begins words of consolation.
days.question: How can you seek the good of the place where you live now?

days.title: A New Covenant
days.intro: Rachel weeps for her children, but God promises their return. He will make a new covenant, writing his law on their hearts and remembering their sins no more. While confined during the siege, Jeremiah buys a field, a pledge that life will go on in the land.
days.question: What would it mean for God’s law to be written on your heart?

days.title: The Burned Scroll
days.intro: God promises healing and a just Branch from David. Judah’s leaders free their slaves, then take them back. The Rechabites’ faithfulness to their ancestor’s rule shames Judah. When King Jehoiakim cuts up and burns Jeremiah’s scroll, Baruch writes it all down again.
days.question: Which of God’s words would you rather cut away and forget?

days.title: Jeremiah in the Cistern
days.intro: Accused of deserting, Jeremiah is jailed, then lowered into a muddy cistern. Ebed-melech, an Ethiopian at the court, rescues him. Zedekiah secretly asks his counsel but will not obey. Jerusalem falls, Zedekiah is blinded, and Jeremiah is freed to stay with the governor Gedaliah.
days.question: Who might need you to speak up for them when others stay silent?

days.title: Flight into Egypt
days.intro: Ishmael murders Gedaliah, and the frightened survivors ask Jeremiah to seek God’s will, promising to obey. God tells them to stay in Judah. They refuse, flee to Egypt, and take Jeremiah with them. There they go on burning incense to the queen of heaven.
days.question: When have you asked for God’s guidance while already set on your own plan?

days.title: A Word for Baruch
days.intro: A short, tender word comes to Baruch: do not seek great things for yourself, and God will spare your life. Then the oracles against the nations begin: Egypt defeated at Carchemish, the Philistines, and proud Moab. Even so, God promises Moab a future restoration.
days.question: What great things for yourself might God be asking you to let go of?

days.title: Babylon Will Fall
days.intro: Judgment comes on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Elam. Then Jeremiah turns to Babylon itself, the empire that crushed Judah. It will be overthrown, and the people of Israel and Judah will come back weeping, seeking the Lord and an everlasting covenant.
days.question: Where do you need to trust God to set right what others have crushed?

days.title: The Last Word on Jerusalem
days.intro: Babylon’s idols will be shamed and its walls brought down. Jeremiah sends a scroll to Babylon to be read aloud and then sunk in the Euphrates. The book closes by retelling Jerusalem’s fall, with one small sign of hope: King Jehoiachin released from prison.
days.question: What small sign of hope has God given you in a hard season?

days.title: Great Is Your Faithfulness
days.intro: Jeremiah sits weeping over the ruined city. These poems, arranged by the letters of the Hebrew alphabet, name grief honestly, and Jerusalem asks passersby if any sorrow is like hers. In chapter 3, at the darkest point, hope breaks through: God’s mercies are new every morning.
days.question: What grief do you need to name honestly before God?

days.title: Confession in Exile
days.intro: Lamentations ends with a plea for God to turn his people back to himself. In Baruch, the exiles in Babylon weep, gather money, and send it to Jerusalem with a humble confession: justice belongs to God, shame to us. The psalm, too, confesses Israel’s sins.
days.question: What would an honest confession of your own sins sound like today?

days.title: Where Wisdom Is Found
days.intro: The exiles ask why they live in a foreign land: they forsook the fountain of wisdom. A poem asks who has found wisdom. God alone knows her way and has given her to Israel in his law. Then Jerusalem speaks as a mother, promising her children’s return.
days.question: Where are you looking for wisdom, and where does God want you to find it?

days.title: Idols That Cannot Save
days.intro: Jerusalem is told to take off her robe of mourning and watch her children return, as God levels the mountains before them. Chapter 6, the Letter of Jeremiah, mocks Babylon’s idols: they cannot speak or see, and must be guarded from rust and thieves.
days.question: What powerless thing do you sometimes treat as if it could save you?

days.title: Ezekiel Sees God’s Glory
days.intro: By the river Chebar in Babylon, the priest Ezekiel sees storm and fire, four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, and the glory of the Lord on a throne. He eats a scroll sweet as honey, is made a watchman, and acts out Jerusalem’s siege.
days.question: How do you respond when God’s word is both sweet and difficult?

days.title: The Mark on the Forehead
days.intro: Ezekiel shaves his head and divides the hair as a sign of coming judgment. In a vision he is carried to Jerusalem and shown idolatry inside the temple itself. A man with a writer’s case marks the foreheads of those who grieve over the city’s sins, and they are spared.
days.question: Do the sins around you still grieve you, or have you grown used to them?

days.title: A Heart of Flesh
days.intro: The glory of the Lord rises from the temple and leaves the city, a terrible moment. Yet God promises the exiles a new spirit, replacing their heart of stone with a heart of flesh. Ezekiel packs an exile’s bag as a sign and condemns prophets who whitewash a flimsy wall.
days.question: Where has your heart turned to stone, and how might God soften it?

days.title: The Foundling Bride
days.intro: Even Noah, Daniel and Job could not save this city by their goodness. Jerusalem is a vine fit only for burning. In a long, startling parable God finds Jerusalem as an abandoned newborn, raises and marries her, and grieves her unfaithfulness. Yet he promises an everlasting covenant.
days.question: How has God cared for you since your earliest days?

days.title: Turn and Live
